help.intro: Twelve sentences describing a room, to listen to and repeat — all on the dative side of the two-way rule, because describing where things are — your flat to a new friend, a room to a flatmate — is what you actually do with it. Das Bett steht an der Wand. Der Tisch steht am Fenster. Say the contractions as one word (am, im) and land the noun with its dative article clearly: an der Wand, auf dem Tisch, unter dem Tisch. One phrase for existence rounds it off: Es gibt auch einen großen Schrank — es gibt always takes the accusative, whatever the room.
help.tips[0].text: Describing where things are: steht / liegt / hängt + an der, auf dem, im, neben dem. Say the article clearly; it carries the case, and the case carries the meaning.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: The bed stands against the wall. A picture hangs above the bed.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: There is a rug under the table.
help.tips[0].check.q: Der Spiegel hängt an ____ Tür. (die Tür)
help.tips[0].check.why: hängt says where something is (wo?), so an takes the dative: die Tür → an der Tür.
help.tips[1].text: In meinem Zimmer gibt es einen Schrank, ein Bett und zwei Stühle. es gibt introduces what exists and always takes the accusative.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: There is also a big wardrobe.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: In the kitchen there's a table and a fridge.
help.tips[1].check.q: In meinem Zimmer gibt es ____ Sessel. (der Sessel)
help.tips[1].check.why: es gibt always takes the accusative, and a masculine noun shows it: einen Sessel.
help.tips[2].title: Tour the room clockwise
help.tips[2].text: Start at the door and go round: Links steht …, an der Wand hängt …, am Fenster steht …, rechts ist … Order gives you fluency.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: To the left, next to the door, stands the wardrobe. The table is by the window.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: The bed is against the wall. A picture hangs above the bed.
help.tips[2].check.why: steht describes position, so it's the dative: an dem → am Fenster. ans would be movement.
help.remember[0]: steht / liegt / hängt + dative: an der, auf dem, im.
help.exam: Describing your room or flat is a typical speaking task in the A2 exam — and the first thing a new neighbour or flatmate asks about.
help.hook: Show someone your room in German: say where the bed, the table and the pictures are — an der Wand, am Fenster.
phrases[2].translation: To the left, next to the door, stands the wardrobe.
phrases[3].translation: The bed is against the wall.
phrases[4].translation: A picture hangs above the bed.
phrases[5].translation: The table is by the window.
phrases[6].translation: There is a book on the table.
phrases[7].translation: There is a lamp next to the bed.
phrases[8].translation: There is a rug under the table.
phrases[9].translation: There is also a big wardrobe.
phrases[10].translation: There are many books on the shelf.
phrases[11].translation: I find my room very cosy.
help.tips[0].title: Position = dative
help.tips[1].title: es gibt + accusative
